specs.title: Dispatcher Cache Interface (Memory-Tier Architecture)
aligned: Edge cases: populate-full, evict exhaustion, concurrent lookups, SSD-full write-through, unpersisted skip, SSD-evictor all-pinned, SSD-evictor order, partition guard

drifted.spec_text: evicts ALL entries ... by calling IMemoryTier::evict_next() in a loop until empty ... convert_memory_tier_to_block. If the transition fails (write-through not complete), the entry is removed from the dispatch map entirely. Returns the number of entries cleared.
drifted.actual: oldest_keys(64+pinned) loop; try_evict_to_block; ActiveReferences (on demote or on the fallback dm.remove) keeps the slot and retries; count only really-cleared; Timeout after 5 s without progress

drifted.spec_text: it is refused while the entry is pinned or write-locked ... A remove that is refused because the entry is pinned returns KeyNotFound and frees nothing.
drifted.actual: the pending write-through's pin is taken over (entry removed; running job frees slot+extent); only a reader/client pin, write lock or lookup timeout yields KeyNotFound

drifted.spec_text: The background writer holds a read reference on each entry while write-through is in progress. The reference is released after write completes or fails.
drifted.actual: only copy_gpu_to_memory_completed jobs hold one (ledger-recorded); remove may take it over; schedule_write_through jobs hold none

drifted.spec_text: MUST use appropriate read/write locking on the dispatch map to ensure thread safety during concurrent operations.
drifted.actual: schedule_write_through job takes no pin (JobStart::Untracked) but settles with convert_to_storage/release_read, decrementing a concurrent reader's pin; reads the slot unpinned so remove/clear can free it under the NVMe write

drifted.spec_text: Cache removal frees all associated resources (memory-tier slots and SSD extents) so that they can be reused.
drifted.actual: remove of a MemoryTier entry with ssd_offset frees no extent (LookupResult::MemoryTier carries no offset); extent leaks and with format_on_init=false the key is recovered at next start

drifted.spec_text: re-insert the entry into the memory-tier and re-register it as a MemoryTier entry
drifted.actual: no-drives promote_and_serve: create_memory_tier_entry on existing entry -> AlreadyExists ignored; stray release_write

drifted.spec_text: reserves refused because the key was already cached
drifted.actual: counted in evict_and_insert for load-path race losers too; now also for a re-store while a removed write-through still holds the slot

partially_implemented.gap: (a) remove_entry give-back window releases the job's pin before re-taking it; a concurrent remove/clear can free the slot under the running job, whose convert_to_storage then fails and leaks the published extent; take_read can block under the ledger mutex. (b) after remove returns with job_frees_slot, a re-store of the key fails AlreadyExists until the job finishes.
clear_memory_tier frees reserved-but-not-completed slots (no dispatch-map entry -> KeyNotFound treated as cleared) while the caller's D2H may be in flight; count includes them

not_verifiable: Edge case: write-ref downgrade lets a concurrent lookup proceed

drifted.spec_text: every key whose copy was in flight is attributed ERROR and none is reported as a hit
drifted.actual: warm batched sync failure only logged; keys stay Ok/Dram

drifted.spec_text: Each attribution value MUST have a test that fails if that value is mis-assigned
drifted.actual: value-specific tests only for Dram and Miss
